shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of B, A, and C. Trading away my A for another B would make me have 2 B and 0 A, reducing variety and lowering my utility since I value balanced holdings. I should reject this trade.
I currently have equal amounts of B, A, and C (1 each). Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and utility since I value balanced holdings.

This trade would leave me with 0 B, 3 A, 1 C - a very unbalanced bundle since I value variety. Giving up my only B for more A (which I already have) reduces diversity. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade for C instead.

This trade would leave me with B:2, A:1, C:0, making my inventory less diverse and reducing utility since I'd have zero of C. Since I currently have equal amounts (1 each), trading away my only C for a second B doesn't improve variety.

Trading away my only B to get a second C would leave me with 0 B, 1 A, 2 C — reducing variety and giving up a good I only have one of, in exchange for more of a good I already have equal amount of. This decreases my utility since I'd go from an even 1-1-1 spread to an unbalanced 0-1-2 bundle.

Trading away my only B (giving up my last unit of a good, going to 0) for 2C would leave me with 0 B, 1 A, 3 C - highly imbalanced. I value variety, so losing my only B unit while stacking up C is a bad trade for my utility.

This trade would give me 2×B and 0×A, going from a balanced 1-1-1 inventory to an unbalanced one, which decreases utility given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep my current balanced bundle or trade for something that maintains diversity.

Current inventory is B:1, A:1, C:1 - perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with B:0, A:1, C:3, which is heavily skewed toward C and eliminates variety in B. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility rather than improving it.

Currently I have 0 B, 1 A, 2 C. Trading my only A for a B would give me 1 B, 0 A, 2 C - still uneven. But since I value variety, having 0 of both A and B is worse than having 1 of each spread differently. Actually let's check: current bundle (0,1,2) vs after (1,0,2). Both have a 0 and a 1 and a 2, so total variety-adjusted value is symmetric - equal utility. Since it's neutral, I'll accept to keep flexibility since B is a good I currently completely lack, and this diversifies risk while it's not worse than before, and opens door for further trades to get A back later while holding C as buffer.
I currently have 0 B and 2 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B moves me toward a more balanced inventory (B:1, A:1, C:1), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

This trade would leave me with 0 C and only 1 B, giving me B:1, A:1, C:0 - trading away all my C for just 1 B creates a new zero-holding, which is worse for variety. Giving up 2 C for 1 B is too steep a ratio; I'd rather trade 1 C for 1 B to maintain balance.

Currently I have 0 B, 1 A, 2 C. Trading my only A for a B gives me 1 B, 0 A, 2 C, which just shifts scarcity from B to A without improving diversity overall. But since I value variety and currently have zero B (most scarce), gaining a B while losing my only A keeps total variety similar (still one good at 0). However, since B is currently more scarce for me than A, moving to have B instead of A doesn't worsen my situation, and having some B could open better future trades to balance all three goods. It's a neutral-to-positive move toward eventually balancing my inventory since B was completely absent."
